key_insight: CT foundation model embeddings predicted distant metastasis risk in head and neck cancer better than radiomics or deep-learning features alone, while requiring less manual region-of-interest work.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier risk stratification from routine preoperative CT scans with less annotation burden, potentially making model deployment more scalable.
method: Used preoperative CT scans from 2,327 patients in the RADCURE dataset.
Extracted three feature sets: radiomics, deep-learning features, and CT Foundation embeddings.
Trained a multilayer perceptron to predict distant metastasis risk and compared performance across feature sets.
evidence_signal: The CT Foundation model achieved an AUC of 0.791, outperforming radiomics (0.772) and deep-learning features (0.753), and performing similarly to the combined-feature model (0.794).
watch_item: The result is promising but comes from a single retrospective dataset, so external validation and prospective testing are still needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Comparing the Performance of Foundation Model Derived Embeddings with Traditional Approaches for Distant Metastasis Prediction in Head and Neck Cancer
